genomeOverview.tagline: I translate user pain into engineering priorities, business metrics into product strategy, and chaos into roadmaps.

genes.name: Product Strategy
genes.expression: I define where we're going and why it matters. Vision � Strategy � Roadmap � OKRs. Every feature ladders up to company goals, or it doesn't ship.
evidence: Defined 3-year product vision adopted by exec team
Restructured roadmap around user outcomes, not feature requests
Killed 40% of backlog items that didn't align with strategy

genes.name: Data Analysis & Metrics
genes.expression: I live in Amplitude, Mixpanel, and SQL queries. Every hypothesis gets measured. Every launch gets a dashboard. Numbers inform decisions, but don't make them.
evidence: Built analytics framework tracking 50+ product metrics
Run A/B tests with proper statistical significance (no peeking!)
Created exec dashboard showing product health at a glance

genes.name: Stakeholder Management
genes.expression: I translate between disciplines. Explain technical constraints to sales, business goals to engineering, user needs to leadership. Everyone thinks I'm on their side.
evidence: Facilitate weekly cross-functional syncs with 15+ stakeholders
Negotiated roadmap with 5 competing teams, everyone left satisfied
Created 'Product Update' newsletter read by 200+ employees

genes.name: Prioritization Frameworks
genes.expression: I say no to good ideas so we can say yes to great ones. RICE scoring, value vs effort matrices, impact mapping - prioritization is my superpower.
evidence: Implemented RICE framework across 3 product teams
Reduced roadmap from 50 items to 12 high-impact bets
Documented prioritization decisions in public Notion doc

genes.name: Cross-Functional Leadership
genes.expression: I lead without authority. Engineers, designers, marketers - I coordinate teams toward shared goals. Influence through data, empathy, and clear communication.
evidence: Led cross-functional squad of 12 (eng, design, data, marketing)
Shipped 8 major features on time through effective coordination
Team feedback: 'Jordan makes complex projects feel manageable'

genes.name: User Empathy + Business Sense
genes.expression: I balance user needs with business constraints. Won't ship dark patterns, but understand CAC/LTV. The best PMs live in the tension between users and revenue.
evidence: Redesigned paywall: +25% conversion while maintaining NPS of 45
Killed feature users loved but had negative unit economics
Created 'North Star Metric' framework balancing growth + satisfaction

genes.name: Execution Discipline
genes.expression: I run tight standups, track blockers obsessively, and unblock teams fast. Scrum, Kanban, Shape Up - I adapt process to team needs.
evidence: 15-minute standups with clear action items
Avg time to unblock engineers: 4 hours
Shipped 90% of roadmap items on time in 2024

genes.name: Adaptability Under Pressure
genes.expression: I stay calm when roadmaps change, priorities shift, or features flop. Startup life is chaos - I find opportunity in uncertainty.
evidence: Pivoted roadmap 3 times in 6 months without team burnout
Led post-mortem after feature failed, team learned vs blamed
Stayed composed during layoffs, maintained team morale

mutations.title: Engineer � Product Manager
mutations.description: Transitioned from writing code to defining what to build. Traded technical depth for strategic breadth.
mutations.newTrait: Learned to measure success by user impact, not lines of code shipped
evidence: First PM role: shipping velocity dropped 40% but user satisfaction up 30%
Realized 'done' means users can succeed, not 'merged to main'
Started reading Teresa Torres, Marty Cagan, Gibson Biddle

mutations.title: Feature Team � Platform Team
mutations.description: Moved from shipping user-facing features to building tools for internal teams. Learned to treat employees as customers.
mutations.newTrait: Developer experience is user experience; DX problems compound across teams
evidence: Built internal tool that saved eng team 10hrs/week
Learned to measure adoption, not just availability
Started weekly 'office hours' to gather internal feedback

mutations.title: Reactive PM � Strategic PM
mutations.description: Stopped accepting roadmap from leadership and started proposing roadmap based on data + user research.
mutations.newTrait: Earned trust by being right about what NOT to build
evidence: Killed 5 exec-requested features based on user research
All 5 would have failed; execs now ask 'What does Jordan think?'
Promoted to Senior PM after proving strategic judgment

projects.title: Freemium to Premium Pricing Migration
projects.context: Startup offering everything free, burning cash. Needed sustainable business model without killing growth. Board pressure to monetize.
approach: Analyzed usage data: 80% of users never used 'pro' features
Interviewed power users to understand willingness to pay
Designed 3-tier pricing: Free (core features) + Pro + Enterprise
A/B tested pricing page messaging with 5,000 users

outcome.metric: MRR grew from $0 to $120k in 6 months

testimonial.quote: Jordan turned our biggest risk into our biggest success. The pricing strategy is now our competitive moat.
testimonial.author: CEO & Co-Founder

projects.insight: Users don't pay for features, they pay to achieve outcomes faster. Price the value, not the cost.

projects.title: Activation Funnel Optimization
projects.context: Sign-ups growing but only 35% activated (completed onboarding). Growth team blamed product complexity.
approach: Built funnel analysis in Mixpanel: identified 3 major drop-off points
Ran 12 A/B tests over 8 weeks targeting each drop-off
Tested: copy changes, UI simplification, email sequences, in-app guidance
Implemented winner from each test sequentially
projects.insight: Don't optimize the whole funnel at once. Fix one step, measure, repeat. Compound improvements add up.

projects.title: Enterprise vs SMB Roadmap Conflict
projects.context: Sales wanted enterprise features (SSO, RBAC). Existing SMB customers wanted speed + simplicity. Engineering team split between priorities.
approach: Facilitated roadmap planning session with sales, CS, eng, design
Created prioritization matrix: Revenue potential � User impact � Effort
Documented trade-offs transparently in public Notion page

outcome.secondary: SMB churn stayed flat (no retention hit)

testimonial.quote: Jordan got us aligned when I thought it was impossible. Everyone understood the why behind priorities.
testimonial.author: VP Sales

projects.insight: Stakeholder management isn't about making everyone happy - it's about making trade-offs explicit and fair.

projects.title: Technical Debt vs Feature Development Balance
projects.context: Engineering team drowning in tech debt. Product team demanding new features. Velocity slowing. Morale tanking.
approach: Quantified tech debt impact: 40% of sprints spent on bugs/maintenance
Proposed 'Innovation Tokens' framework: 20% every sprint for debt
Tracked velocity over time to prove investment paid off
Made tech debt visible to stakeholders in roadmap reviews

testimonial.quote: Jordan made tech debt a first-class citizen. Our codebase is healthier and we ship faster.
testimonial.author: Engineering Lead

projects.insight: Tech debt is product work. If engineers are the only ones who care, you're managing wrong.

uniqueSequence.statement: I balance user needs, business goals, and technical constraints to ship products that matter.
whyRare: Most PMs lean analytics OR empathy, not both equally
Most strategists struggle with execution; most executors lack vision
Most diplomats avoid hard prioritization calls; I make trade-offs explicit
evidence: Balanced Big Five scores (no trait above 71 or below 48)
Shipped products that hit user satisfaction AND revenue targets
Led teams through pivots without burnout or attrition

excel.name: 0-to-1 Product Development
excel.basis: Strategic thinking + user empathy + high tolerance for ambiguity
excel.inPractice: Thrive when building new products from scratch; love discovery and iteration
excel.bestApplied: Early-stage startups; new product initiatives; innovation teams

excel.name: Cross-Functional Team Leadership
excel.basis: Balanced personality = can relate to diverse working styles
excel.inPractice: Bridge gaps between eng (detail-oriented), design (creative), sales (results-driven)
excel.bestApplied: Teams with strong individual contributors who need coordination, not micromanagement

excel.name: Metrics-Driven Organizations
excel.basis: Love of data + discipline around measurement
excel.inPractice: Shine in companies that make decisions based on evidence, not HiPPO opinions
excel.bestApplied: Growth-stage startups; data-mature orgs like Stripe, Amplitude, Notion

capable.name: Mature Enterprise Products
capable.basis: Can manage complexity but miss the creativity of early-stage
capable.inPractice: Effective at optimization and scaling, but energized more by innovation
capable.bestApplied: Growth phase vs maintenance phase; optimization projects with clear goals

capable.name: Technical Product Management
capable.basis: Engineering background helps but not deeply technical anymore
capable.inPractice: Can read code, understand architecture, but need eng partner for deep technical decisions
capable.bestApplied: Developer tools, APIs, platforms - with strong technical co-founder or lead

capable.name: High-Pressure Sales-Driven Culture
capable.basis: Can handle pressure but prefer balanced approach to product development
capable.inPractice: Effective at shipping fast when needed, but sustainable pace produces better outcomes
capable.bestApplied: Quarterly deadlines over monthly fire drills; strategic over reactive

developing.name: Long-Term Vision (3-5 years)
developing.basis: Strong at 6-18 month roadmaps; developing multi-year strategic thinking
developing.myApproach: Reading Gibson Biddle, Shreyas Doshi; working with mentor on vision frameworks
developing.growth: Improved from quarterly thinking to annual planning; working toward 3-year vision

developing.name: Saying No Without Over-Explaining
developing.basis: Tend to justify decisions with data; learning brevity and confidence
developing.myApproach: 'No because...' � 'No, and here's what we're prioritizing instead'
developing.growth: Reduced PRD length by 40%; learning when more context hurts clarity

developing.name: Design Intuition
developing.basis: Strong at product logic, still building design taste and craft knowledge
developing.myApproach: Partner closely with designers; studying great product design; building side projects
developing.growth: Can now give useful design feedback; working toward having design point of view

thrivingEnvironments.title: Data-Informed, User-Centric Culture
thrivingEnvironments.why: Need balance: metrics inform decisions but user insights drive direction

thrivingEnvironments.title: Cross-Functional Respect & Collaboration
thrivingEnvironments.why: Thrive when PM, Eng, Design have equal voice; struggle in hierarchical orgs

thrivingEnvironments.title: Outcome Over Output Focus
thrivingEnvironments.why: Love teams that measure impact (retention, satisfaction) not just velocity (features shipped)

strugglingEnvironments.title: Feature Factories
strugglingEnvironments.why: Burn out when treated as roadmap administrator vs strategic partner

strugglingEnvironments.title: HiPPO-Driven Decision Making
strugglingEnvironments.why: Frustrated when data/research ignored for Highest Paid Person's Opinion

strugglingEnvironments.title: Siloed Organizations
strugglingEnvironments.why: Can't be effective PM when eng, design, sales don't talk to each other

compatibility.idealHabitat: Growth-stage startup (Series A-C) with data-informed culture, cross-functional collaboration, outcome-focused metrics, and room for strategic PM influence. Bonus: user research budget and engineering that values product partnership.
